claims.text: Spark plasma sintering can produce HfNbTaTiZr as a single-phase random solid solution.
Spark plasma sintering achieved an oxygen content of approximately 0.12 wt% in HfNbTaTiZr.
The spark-plasma-sintered HfNbTaTiZr specimen is defect-free.
Random atomic arrangements in HfNbTaTiZr produce intrinsic force-constant fluctuations.
An on-the-fly MLFF calibrated with ab initio data can explicitly capture force-constant disorder and anharmonic phonon-scattering dynamics in HfNbTaTiZr.
Force-constant disorder dominates phonon scattering in these alloys.
The MLFF approach will calculate lattice thermal conductivity independently of electronic thermal transport.
Earlier Debye-based or simple DFT approaches conflate lattice and electronic thermal conductivity.
The proposed method will predict lattice thermal conductivity 20–30% more accurately than the baseline approaches.
Below 200 K, the lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions of HfNbTaTiZr are comparable.
The lattice thermal conductivity of HfNbTaTiZr will be nearly temperature-invariant below 200 K.
The lattice thermal conductivity of HfNbTaTiZr will increase modestly at elevated temperatures.
Earlier conductivity calculations generally represent perfect, defect-free bulk crystals.
The proposed predictions are applicable from below 200 K through 1200 K.
The hypothesis is valid for single-phase HfNbTaTiZr with no more than 0.2 wt% oxygen and minimal extrinsic scattering.
Significant oxygen contamination or secondary phases can invalidate the transport prediction by altering scattering mechanisms.
Simple fluctuation-based analytical phonon models fail to reproduce all directional behavior and therefore require more complex modeling.
Applying a magnetic field can suppress the electronic thermal-conductivity contribution sufficiently to isolate the lattice contribution.
Low-temperature measurements provide a clearer separation of lattice and electronic thermal transport.
